source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.campus_mw_context: The 128,715-sq. ft. data center in Sterling, VA, offers 11 MW of IT capacity and features robust connectivity options with high bandwidth and high-availability circuits and a number of metro and long-haul networks.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA4's 11 MW is under 1% of the 1,603 MW that Virginia's 25 capacity-publishing data centers disclose, and 305 of the state's 330 mapped facilities publish no capacity at all.

The disclosed Virginia total is a floor, not a census. Of 330 mapped data centers, 25 report a capacity figure, and those 25 sum to 1,603 MW. An 11 MW campus is therefore marginal to the state's published aggregate. The data also places NVA4 26th among Virginia facilities with published capacity, which cannot be reconciled with only 25 facilities publishing a figure. Treat that rank as unresolved rather than as a finding.

Power is the number that governs AI scaling, and 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet is small. At the stated assumption of 40 kW per rack, that is roughly 275 racks. The facility's distinguishing feature in the data is network reach, with multiple metro and long-haul circuits. That addresses data movement for distributed workloads, not the power ceiling that limits training at scale. On the evidence here, this site reads as enterprise, inference, or specialized compute rather than frontier model development.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. There is no total facility load, no efficiency figure, no utilization, no utility or interconnection detail, and no on-site generation. The 305 mapped Virginia facilities without published capacity could include larger campuses nearby, so nothing here establishes the state's true aggregate capacity or this site's place in it.
